newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets 1997 targets for grain, cotton.
newsitem.headline: China sets 1997 targets for grain, cotton.

text.p: China's agricultural authorities have set a base target for grain production in 1997 of 480 million tonnes, around the same level as the estimated record output this year, the People's Daily said on Friday.
Farmers should work to achieve some increase over 1996 output next year, the official newspaper quoted Minister of Agriculture Liu Jiang as saying, but gave no details.
Grain production should be at the heart of agricultural work in 1997 and the area planted with grain should be guaranteed at the 1996 level of 112 million hectares, Liu said.

The target for 1997 output of cotton was set at 4.25 million tonnes, he said. China's official forecast for the 1996 cotton harvest is 3.5 million tonnes, down more than 1.0 million tonnes from 1995 because of low state-set prices that made many farmers shift to other crops.
Officials say Beijing may use market forces to govern cotton prices next year.
The People's Daily quoted Liu as setting a 1997 target for output of meat products at 62 million tonnes, up from an estimated 58 million tonnes this year.
Output of aquatic products should reach 31 million tonnes, up from an expected 28 million tonnes in 1996, he said.

The value of agricultural output should grow 4.0 percent compared with an estimated rise of 4.5 percent in 1996, while farmers income should grow 5.0 percent in real terms -- the same level as was expected this year, he said.

The target for output growth from village and township enterprises -- one of the most vigorous sectors in the Chinese economy -- was 15 percent, down slightly from an estimated 16.5 percent in 1996, he said.
